title: Reversible and irreversible card sort
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Changes of materials and animals including humans
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 24 (Reversible and irreversible card sort (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 24: Changes of materials: consolidation and results. To understand how to decide whether any change is reversible or irreversible using evidence

blocks.title: Sort into: Reversible / Irreversible
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Reversible, Irreversible.
blocks.answer: Reversible: Melting ice; Dissolving sugar; Freezing juice; Evaporating water; Melting wax. Irreversible: Baking bread; Rusting nail; Burning wood; Frying an egg; Milk going sour

questions.q: Use the table: which conditions made the most rust?
questions.model: Read the 'rust' column: 'a lot' is beside salt water. So salt water made the most rust.

questions.q: Which apple slice browned least in your test?
questions.a: Pupils' own; usually the lemon juice or cling film slice

questions.q: Write a conclusion for the rust test in the portal response box: 'Iron needs ... and ... to rust. My evidence is ...'
questions.a: Iron needs water and oxygen to rust. My evidence is the dry jar did not rust and the salt water jar rusted most.
questions.model: Teacher writes the first half for the class: 'Iron needs water and oxygen to rust.'

questions.q: Explain why the candle example is both.
questions.a: Wax melting can set again; burning wax makes new gases and cannot be undone.

questions.q: Suggest how to protect a metal bench in a park near the sea.
questions.a: Paint or galvanise it, because salt water speeds up rusting.

questions.q: Big question: which part of a burning candle is reversible?
questions.a: The melting wax; burning is irreversible.
